1.title: The feast at Shushan
1.text: After the hundred and eighty days, the king holds a further seven-day feast for all the people in the court of the garden of the royal palace at Shushan.

1.question: Where did the king hold the seven-day feast?
options: In the court of the garden of the royal palace, at Shushan
In the hall of the throne of the royal fortress at Shushan
In the inner court of the palace, before the presence of the king
In the banqueting house of the king at Shushan

1.question: Who made a feast for the women in the royal house?
options: Queen Vashti
Queen Esther
The king's mother
Zeresh

1.question: How many princes of Persia and Media saw the king's face?
options: Seven
Three
Twelve
Ten

1.question: According to the ladies, Vashti's deed would bring among the women
options: Too much contempt and wrath
Great gladness and contentment
Peace and harmony among families
Honor and full submission

1.question: What did the king decree by letters to all the provinces?
options: That every man should bear rule in his own house
That all the pagan altars should be entirely torn down
That all the women should bow down before Vashti
That a brand new temple should be built

2.title: Seeking a new queen
2.text: With the king's wrath appeased, his servants propose gathering fair young virgins; the one who pleased the king would reign in Vashti's place.

2.question: Who would reign in Vashti's place?
options: The maiden who pleased the king
The princess, daughter of the king of Media and Persia
Mordecai's wife, chosen in secret
Esther's own cousin, Haman's daughter

2.question: How did Hegai, keeper of the women, treat Esther?
options: She obtained kindness and was preferred to the best place of the house of the women
She was completely rejected by Hegai and sent back to her father's own house
She was placed among the lesser concubines of the royal house, entirely without honor
She was sent back to her father's house immediately, without any honor

2.question: Whose daughter was Esther?
options: Abihail's, the uncle of Mordecai
King Ahasuerus's own, her royal husband
Haman's, the Agagite enemy of the Jews
Memucan's, wise counselor to the king

2.question: Where was Mordecai sitting?
options: In the king's gate
In the temple
In the palace garden
In Haman's house

2.question: What happened to the two chamberlains who plotted against the king?
options: They were both hanged on a tree
They were pardoned by King Ahasuerus himself
They fled to Babylon together with their families
They were made princes of the realm

3.title: Haman's wrath
3.text: Haman, exalted by the king, is full of wrath because Mordecai will not bow; he resolves to destroy not only Mordecai but all the Jews in the kingdom.

3.question: What did Haman seek to do when he learned Mordecai was a Jew?
options: Destroy all the Jews in the kingdom of Ahasuerus
Pardon Mordecai and raise him to second in the realm
Flee the city of Shushan with all his family and friends
Apologize humbly to the king for his pride

3.question: What did the king give Haman when he agreed to his plan?
options: His ring
His crown
His sword
His throne

3.question: How was the city of Shushan when the decree was proclaimed?
options: Perplexed
Glad
Empty
Feasting

4.title: Mordecai's mourning
4.text: Learning of the decree, Mordecai puts on sackcloth and ashes and cries through the city; Esther, on hearing of it, is exceedingly grieved.

4.question: How did Mordecai react when he learned of the decree?
options: He put on sackcloth and ashes and cried through the city
He immediately fled to Ethiopia, taking his whole family
He went directly to speak with Haman, begging urgently for mercy
He held a great feast with all his closest friends

4.question: Who brought Mordecai's words to Esther?
options: Hatach, the king's chamberlain
The king himself, coming in person
Haman, the sworn enemy of the Jews
Zeresh, Haman's own wife

4.question: What did Mordecai warn Esther about her own danger?
options: That she would not escape in the king's house more than the other Jews
That she was entirely safe as the rightfully and lawfully chosen queen
That she must flee the palace before dawn with her loyal maidens of trust
That she must reveal everything to Haman at once to save herself

4.question: What did Mordecai do after Esther's answer?
options: He did according to all that Esther had commanded him
He refused to help her at all and stormed off angrily
He left for Jerusalem at once without saying another word
He was arrested at once by the king's own guards

5.title: Esther's first banquet
5.text: The king receives Esther and, eager for her request, calls for Haman to make haste and come to the banquet she had prepared.

5.question: Whom did Esther invite to her banquet along with the king?
options: Haman
Mordecai
Vashti
Memucan

5.question: Whom did Haman call for when he came home?
options: His friends and Zeresh his wife
The king and Queen Esther together
Mordecai and the elders of the Jews
The satraps of India and Persia

5.question: What did Zeresh and his friends advise Haman to do?
options: Have a gallows made to hang Mordecai
Ask Mordecai's forgiveness in front of everyone
Leave the city of Shushan forever that very night
Give away his riches to the poor of the city

6.title: The sleepless night
6.text: Unable to sleep, the king has the chronicles read and discovers that Mordecai, who had exposed the plot, had never been honored.

6.question: Who entered the court just as the king sought how to honor Mordecai?
options: Haman
Mordecai
Harbonah
Memucan

6.question: To whom did the king command Haman to render the honor he had described?
options: To Mordecai the Jew
To himself, Haman
To Queen Esther
To the chamberlains

6.question: Where did the chamberlains hasten Haman at the chapter's end?
options: To the banquet Esther had prepared
To the gallows he himself had built
To the king's palace for a new decree
To his own house in deep disgrace

7.title: Esther reveals her people
7.text: At the second banquet, Esther asks the king for her own life and that of her people, declaring they have been sold to be destroyed.

7.question: What did Esther declare had happened to her and her people?
options: They were sold to be destroyed, slain, and to perish
That they would only be reduced to slavery in the farthest lands
That they would receive pardon from the king for a grand ransom of gold
That they would be exiled forever from the lands of Persia

7.question: What happened to Haman at the end of the chapter?
options: He was hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai
He was exiled far away to Babylon by order of king Ahasuerus
He was appointed governor over the fortress of Shushan
He fled far away with his whole family to escape

8.title: Esther's plea
8.text: Esther falls at the king's feet and begs him to reverse Haman's device, for she cannot endure to see the evil that shall come to her people.

8.question: Why was Esther pleading with the king?
options: She could not endure to see the evil that shall come to her people
She wanted to receive for herself all the wealth and lands of Haman
She desired that Mordecai be appointed vice-regent over the empire
She wanted personally to avenge herself on all her oppressors

8.question: On what day could the Jews defend themselves, by the new decree?
options: On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month Adar
On the first and last day of the tenth month, the month of Tebeth
On the last day of the seventh month, called the month of Tishri
In the month of Nisan, at the beginning of the year

8.question: What did many of the people of the land do because of the fear of the Jews?
options: They became Jews
They fled the kingdom
They attacked the Jews
They worshipped Haman

9.title: Mordecai's greatness
9.text: On the day the enemies hoped to overpower the Jews, the opposite came to pass; and Mordecai waxed greater and greater in the king's house.

9.question: How was Mordecai in the king's house?
options: Great, and his fame went throughout all the provinces
Humble, and hardly anyone in Shushan knew his true name
Hated, and greatly feared only within the walls of Shushan
Unknown beyond the limits of the royal palace

9.question: What did the Jews NOT do after slaying Haman's ten sons?
options: They laid not their hand on the spoil
They did not divide the spoil among the poor
They did not burn the bodies of Haman's sons
They did not ask the king for pardon

9.question: How many men did the Jews of Shushan slay on the fourteenth of Adar?
options: Three hundred
Five hundred
Seventy-five thousand
Ten

9.question: What did the Jews of the villages make of the fourteenth of Adar?
options: A day of gladness, feasting, and sending portions one to another
A day of fasting, mourning, and asking forgiveness one from another
A day of forced labor and paying tribute to the governor of the region
A day of silence and quiet retreat in their own homes

9.question: What happened to Haman's wicked device, according to the king's letters?
options: It returned upon his own head, and he and his sons were hanged
He was executed at once by the king without harm to his family
It was made into royal decree and instantly enforced against the Jewish people
It was completely canceled and never mentioned again

9.question: What confirmed the matters of that Purim and was written in the book?
options: The decree of Esther
The edict of Mordecai
The register of the satraps
The book of Shushan

10.title: Mordecai, second in the kingdom
10.text: Mordecai becomes second only to king Ahasuerus, great among the Jews, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace for all his nation.

10.question: What was Mordecai's position at the end of the book?
options: Next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews
A humble scribe, forgotten by most of the Jewish people
An exiled governor, without any power in the Persian court
A forgotten servant in the distant lands of Media
